original.target_description: Unassigned original side; not assessed in this source-grouped completion.

replication.target_description: Revised protocol in current Many Labs 5 project: expressed anger versus happiness predicting initial chips offered, low consequences of rejection, after preregistered exclusions; Table 2 descriptive difference and Table 4 protocol-specific mixed-effects emotion test with testing-site random intercept.

n.sample_role: Participants included in the post-exclusion target protocol analysis; all received low-consequences instructions. Not recruitment total, sites, or testing groups.
n.exclusions: 157 subjects (57%) excluded from the revised protocol by preregistered criteria; final 119. Criteria: knowledge of the ultimatum game, doubt that partner was real, familiarity with other subjects, and failed manipulation check. Five additional enrolled subjects could not be tested source-wide; allocation unspecified.

notes: Identity verified from supplied canonical publisher-PDF text: title Many Labs 5: Replication of van Dijk, van Kleef, Steinel, and van Beest (2008); Lauren Skorb and coauthors including Joshua K. Hartshorne; DOI 10.1177/2515245920927643; AMPPS 2020, 3(3), 418–428. Primary empirical registered report, with overlapping line-numbered extracts extending through references, not abstract-only. No local PDF was assigned, so no rendering was possible. Target matched using named protocol, initial-offer outcome, low consequences and post-exclusion Table 2, not row order or numerical matching. N is explicitly printed final included sample, no arithmetic derivation. Table 2 prints signed Cohen’s d for the angry-minus-happy difference; retained as printed. Table 4 supplies protocol-specific mixed-effects p and Wald z for the same outcome/sample/emotion contrast, coding happy relative to angry and including testing-site random intercept; d is descriptive, not a standardized regression coefficient or a converted z. Table 3 interaction tests and Table 5/6 analyses retaining subjects who believed partner was a computer are distinct and not used. Narrative classification follows authors’ stated successful-replication criterion and statement that only the revised protocol provided significant support; all protocols were in original direction. Original side is an unassigned placeholder and must not overwrite prior original extraction.
